title: Concrete Pump for Slope and Retaining-Wall Placement
seoTitle: Concrete Pump for Slope Retaining Wall | Pinjin Xingtai
description: Use the printed vertical and horizontal metres on the Pinjin row — Electric 15 lists 15–20 m vertical; Electric 40 lists 120 m / 360 m (fine stone). Pinjin does not print a slope angle or retaining-wall certificate. Pipeline equivalent length still applies. Match the row, then inquire.

answerBlock.what: Slope and retaining-wall pours still read the catalogue vertical and horizontal cells. Electric 15: 60–80 m / 15–20 m. Electric 40: fine-stone 120 m / 360 m, 23 MPa. Diesel 40 lists 66 kW, 26 m³/h, 120 m / 360 m — a diesel row, not an Electric 40 twin. Pinjin does not print a slope angle, batter or retaining-wall formwork-pressure certificate. Equivalent-length rules are on the vertical-vs-horizontal and high-rise pages — we will not invent a ‘15° slope = N metres’ table. Prime the line; a dry reducer on an uphill hose plugs the same way as on a slab.
answerBlock.who: Buyers placing concrete up a bank or into a retaining-wall form who can measure vertical rise and pipe length, not buyers asking for an unpublished angle chart.
factors: Use printed vertical m and horizontal m on that model row
No published slope-angle or wall-pressure certificate
Uphill hose still needs priming and DN-matched couplings
Diesel vs electric is a grid fact, not a slope SKU

faqs.question: Does Pinjin rate Electric 15 for a 30-degree slope?
faqs.answer: No slope-angle cell is printed. Electric 15 lists 15–20 m vertical and 60–80 m horizontal. Measure the rise and the pipe length. We will not convert an unpublished 30° into extra metres.

faqs.question: Is a retaining-wall pour the same as a high-rise cell?
faqs.answer: Both read vertical metres, but a wall is not a tower. High-rise selection and vertical-vs-horizontal already explain equivalent length. This page only says: use those printed metres; do not invent a wall certificate. Send form height and line length with the slug.

faqs.question: Should I use Diesel 40 on a remote slope with no grid?
faqs.answer: Diesel 40 is the diesel row (26 m³/h, 66 kW, 120 m / 360 m). Electric 40 is 45 kW, 380V 50Hz. Site power is a fact — see electric vs diesel and diesel no-electricity. Slope angle is still not a catalogue cell on either page.
